name: nsidc-polar-stereo
title: NSIDC polar stereographic sea ice grids (25, 12.5, 6.25 km)
description: One raster per hemisphere on a shared 6.25 km-aligned lattice; untiled. Instances for the original Hughes 1980 CRSs (EPSG:3411/3412, deprecated) and their WGS 84 successors (EPSG:3413/3976), with the same grid numbers.

provenance.derived_from: Tables 5-7 of the NSIDC guide (grid dimensions, corner coordinates) and its projection parameters
notes: Extents are the published grid corners, which are outer pixel edges (304 x 25 km = 7600 km = 3850 + 3750 km).

Hughes 1980 instances, as PROJ strings: +proj=stere +lat_0={lat_0} +lat_ts={lat_ts} +lon_0={lon_0} +k=1 +x_0=0 +y_0=0 +a=6378273 +b=6356889.449 +units=m +no_defs, with lat_0/lat_ts/lon_0 from the instance table.
assign is 'single' as a placeholder: the hemisphere instance is chosen by the user (or by the sign of lat); the north and south grids overlap nowhere, but each datum pair overlaps completely.
The ID template is crsgrid's own; NSIDC names grids by product (psn25 / pss25 files), not by a scheme.
Distinctive for crsgrid: an untiled grid (the common 'one CRS, one extent, one resolution' case), per-instance extents, and deprecated EPSG codes the linter should point at their successors.

superseded_by records NSIDC's guidance that new products use EPSG:3413/3976. EPSG itself has not deprecated 3411/3412 (EPSG v11.022, PROJ 9.5.1 and 9.8.1), so a lint should say 'superseded by NSIDC', not 'deprecated'.

The same grid numbers in the two datums are different grids: the published corner coordinates are the Hughes 1980 values, and under WGS 84 the corners move by about 0.001 degree (roughly 100 m). An alignment lint must not report a 3411 grid and a 3413 grid as aligned.
